rationale.conceptual: The method relies entirely on standard, well-documented DFT techniques (PBE functional, PAW pseudopotentials, slab models, formation energy formula, CI-NEB) with no novel algorithm. Reproducing the paper requires familiarity with computational surface science but no deep mathematical derivation beyond textbook formulas.
rationale.execution: The pipeline includes 6 explicit stages (slab relaxations, cluster relaxations, formation energy analysis, structural preference determination, NEB calculation, barrier reporting) with inter-dependencies and several load-bearing handoffs. While each step is straightforward, orchestrating multiple DFT calculations and collecting results into required CSV/TXT formats adds moderate orchestration complexity.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing standard DFT calculations using established methods (PBE, slab models, formation energy formula, CI-NEB). Conceptually it involves textbook-level density functional theory and surface science, making it a moderate conceptual challenge. The execution pipeline has multiple sequential steps (6 stages) with dependencies and requires careful management of DFT runs, but the tooling is well-defined and the data volume is tiny, so it is moderately complex. Resources are modest because the slab models are small (<500 atoms) and DFT can run on CPUs with moderate memory.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Slab models with ~300-400 atoms and a few cluster configurations fit in typical DFT plane-wave calculations; a single CPU node with 16 GB RAM suffices. No large datasets, just crystal structure files.
